text: NASA/TM-20210011385 47 4.0 Individual Principal Investigator Report: Fernandez-Pello 4.1 Opposed-Flame Spread Task The scientific objective of the Burning and Suppression Solids—II (BASS–II) opposed-flow flame spread test is to further understand the mechanisms controlling the spread of flames over the surface of solid combustible materials, particularly in a spacecraft environment.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For this purpose, experiments were conducted aboard the International Space Station (ISS) to determine the effects of microgravity on the spread of flames over polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) rods of different diameters subjected to different O2 concentrations and low flow velocities.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These are parameters that in addition to low pressure are expected in spacecraft environments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: By conducting these tests aboard the ISS and then comparing the results to ground-based data, it is expected that a better understanding of the governing mechanisms of flame spread in microgravity can be obtained.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition, by conducting the tests with cylindrical samples, the effect on the flame spread process of geometrical factors such as the transverse curvature of the surface can be better studied.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 4.1.1 Experiment and Test Matrix The tests were conducted in the BASS–II hardware placed inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) in the Destiny Lab of the ISS.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The BASS–II hardware consists of a flow duct, still camera, video camera, external control box, and associated plumbing and mounting systems along with the fuel samples for the BASS–II experiments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The tests for the present task were conducted with rods of cast PMMA with diameters of 6.35, 9.525, and 12.7 mm (1/4, 3/8, and 1/2 in., respectively) and were 57.15 mm in length.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: All cylindrical rods tested started with rounded (hemispherical) ends in order to minimize the flow disturbance associated with the abrupt bluff body transition at the sample’s downstream edge.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Ignition of the PMMA was accomplished by using a hot wire placed to heat the PMMA surface in the downstream edge of the rods.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Table 4.1 and Table 4.2 present the test conditions for the opposed-flow flame spread tests conducted in this task.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The majority of the tests were conducted with black PMMA, because rods of black PMMA are also used in the Material Ignition and Suppression Test (MIST) project to reduce effects of in-depth absorption of thermal radiation.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For this reason, the results presented in this report are limited to those for black PMMA.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A few tests were conducted with clear PMMA for comparison purposes, but the data is too limited to present it here.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 4.1.2 Results Multiple test conditions were accomplished for each PMMA sample by igniting the sample at a high opposed-flow velocity and then subsequently reducing the opposed-flow velocity until extinction was observed, pausing along the way to allow steady-state flame spread.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The results presented herein comprise the effects of O2 concentration and flow velocity on the rate of microgravity opposed-flame spread over black PMMA rods in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Figure 4.1(a) presents a summary of the results of the effect of flow velocity on the opposed-flow flame spread rate for 0.00635-, 0.009525-, and 0.0127-mdiameter rods of black cast PMMA.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The data points are at different O2 concentrations, which explains some of the scatter in the data.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As can be seen in Figure 4.1(a), the average flame spread rate increases with opposed-flow velocity, even within the small range of flow velocities tested.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Sustained flame spread for the conditions tested was not observed for opposed-flow velocities below approximately 4 mm/s for the 0.00635- and 0.009525-mdiameter rods.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Visually it was observed that at very low flow velocities the flames appear to be very small, blue, faint, and open at their downstream ends.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As the flow velocity rises towards 20 mm/s and above, the flames become much more luminous, with bright yellow flames, and a closed downstream tip.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In Figure 4.1(b), the data exhibits an upward trend in spread rate with increasing O2 concentration, which is especially marked in the results of the 6.35-mm-diameter rods.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Both of these sets of observations are similar to those of previous work on flame spread in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In comparing the experimental results from ground-based experiments with those conducted aboard the ISS, a number of complications arise.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: First and foremost, due to the effect of buoyancy, the effective opposed-flow velocity felt by the flame in the 1g experiments is an order of magnitude greater than the velocities tested in microgravity experiments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As has been shown elsewhere, the difference in flame spread rate between natural convective conditions and an opposed-flow velocity of 0.25 m/s in 1g is relatively negligible.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: On the other hand, for the microgravity tests presented herein, the flow velocities under investigation are near the quenching limit, below those normally expected from the air supply and recirculation systems currently employed on the ISS.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition to difficulties regarding the use of comparable flow velocities, in the microgravity experiments only the two largest diameter rods were tested at near 21 percent O2 by volume, with the highest O2 concentration tested for the 6.35-mm-diameter rods being approximately 19 percent by volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The only O2 concentration at which all three rod diameters employed in the microgravity experiments were tested was at approximately 17.5 percent O2 by volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In the 1g experiments, the lowest O2 concentration at which all four tested rod diameters were successfully burnt without the addition of an external radiant heat source was 19 percent by volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Thus, in comparing the datasets, some compromises were made.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In particular, as can be seen in Figure 4.3, the ranges of O2 concentrations and rod diameters employed do not completely overlap.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Yet, the trend in flame spread rate in terms of both O2 concentration and rod diameter are still quite apparent even after discounting the fact that the flow velocities are not strictly comparable.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 50 The most important result of the comparison is that of the minimum O2 concentration for flame spread in normal and microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: While in microgravity, flame spread was observed at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, in normal gravity, flame spread was not observed below 19 percent.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This result is probably due to the lower opposed-flow velocity in the microgravity tests in comparison with those induced by buoyancy in normal gravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 55 5.0 Individual Principal Investigator Report: Miller and Wichman 5.1 Narrow Channel Apparatus as Microgravity Flame Spread Surrogate Combustion of clear cast polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) samples 10 cm long by either 1 or 2 cm wide with thicknesses ranging from 1 to 5 mm was investigated in opposed flow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Tests included both one-sided and two-sided burns.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The samples were burned in a flow duct within the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) on the International Space Station (ISS) to ensure true microgravity conditions.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The experiment took place in opposed flow with a varying O2 concentration (uncontrolled) and varying flow velocities (controlled).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Flames are recorded on two cameras and later tracked to determine spread rate.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Assuming a linear profile between O2 concentration at the start and the end of each test, we made graphs of O2 concentration versus time for each test.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: From these, we created flammability maps showing the flame behavior at different O2 concentrations and flow velocities.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Additionally, we have conducted an extinction analysis, plotting the O2 concentration against the flow velocity at the time of extinction with respect to type of test (one sided or two sided).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Currently we are modeling combustion of flat PMMA samples in microgravity using Fire Dynamic Simulator (FDS; v5.5.3; National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The entire modeling for Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS–II) is performed in Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) mode because of the laminar conditions and small domain.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The model employs the same test sample and MSG geometry as the experiment.

text: 5.2 Introduction The NASA Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS–II) tests examine the combustion of different solid materials and geometries in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: While flames in microgravity are driven by diffusion and weak advection due to ventilation systems and crew movement, the current NASA spacecraft material selection test method (NASA–STD–6001 Test 1) (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 1) is driven by buoyant forces since gravity is present.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: So, the BASS–II results will be used in comparison with ground-based experimental setups aimed at replacing NASA’s current test method for screening materials used onboard spacecraft.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The data gathered will also help us understand and know more about behavior of fires in space so that space travel can be made safer in the future.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The BASS–II experiments have provided us with an extensive thick fuel microgravity database that did not exist previously.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Previously, thick-fuel true microgravity data was obtained by Olson and others in a study involving Sounding Rocket experiments (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The study comprised a series of combustion experiments on polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) at very low velocity opposed flow and external radiant flux.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The institutions taking part in BASS–II operations are Case Western Reserve University; University of California, Berkeley; NASA Glenn Research Center; San Diego State University; and Michigan State University (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: There are three categories of samples: flat samples, rod samples, and a section of a large solid sphere.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flat sample materials will include acrylic films and sheets of different thicknesses, and a cotton-fiberglass fabric blend Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low-Speeds (SIBAL) fuel.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The rod samples are made of black or clear acrylic and will provide solid fuel regression rates and extinction limits for both opposed and concurrent flow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The large solid spherical section, also made of acrylic, will be used to study ignition of thick materials and flame growth over the thick material.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 56 5.3 Experimental Setup and Summary The BASS–II hardware shown in Figure 5.1 comprises a small flow duct with an igniter and a small nozzle along with exchangeable fuel samples.

text: A total of 20 PMMA flat samples were burnt during the BASS–II experimentation (Table 5.1).

text: 5.5 Numerical Modeling We are modeling combustion of flat PMMA samples in microgravity using Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS; v5.5.3; National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)) (Ref.

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 63 5.7 Conclusions The Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) experiments gave some of the first ever data regarding combustion of thick fuels in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The two-sided summary graphs show that for thin fuels, sample width affects the spread rate.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In general, the flames spread faster for two-sided burns compared to one-sided burns.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The greater the thickness of the fuel, the greater is the time taken for the flame to spread and so the lower is the spread rate.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This is clearly evident in the different thicknesses that we have tested.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The model currently predicts much higher spread rates than those obtained in the experiment.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: We need to modify chemical kinetics and material properties to improve model accuracy and results.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 6.1.6 Conclusions For the first time, a series of concurrent rod flammability tests were conducted in microgravity aboard the International Space Station (ISS).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A small flow duct was used to create 0- to 55-cm/s flows past the three sizes of clear and black PMMA rods.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Ignition delay time increased significantly as the minimum limiting O2 concentration is approached.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Ignition limits are found to be at higher O2 concentrations than the flammability limits due to the added heat loss to the initially cold fuel rod present at ignition.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The ignition delay time can be up to almost 10 times longer than the NASA STD–6001 standard igniter on time.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Detailed observations of near-quenching flames are described, including flame standoff distance trend with O2 and stretch rate a.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flame shrinks to a hemispherical blue shape just before quenching.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Prequenching extinction oscillations at 1.1 Hz are observed with a radiometer and are similar to previously reported quiescent candle flame oscillations in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As flow speed is increased, blowoff extinction is initiated by the formation of a hole in the flame sheet in the stagnation region of the flame.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Once the stagnation region is blown far enough downstream of the stagnation region (greater than one gas-phase thermal length l), the flame is unable to propagate back upstream even when the flow is reduced.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This is consistent with observations that at the low O2 concentrations of interest, an opposed-flow flame cannot be established.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Blowoff extinction limits from the ISS experiments agree well with Zero Gravity Research Facility 5.18-s drop test limits.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The lower portion of the flammability boundary, with O2 concentration and a as coordinates, was outlined as stochastic region between stable flames and extinguished flames.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A curve fit including an exponential and linear term was used to empirically define the boundary.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The minimum in the flammability boundary is at a of 8 to 12 s–1, where the a is modified to account for the various rod sizes tested through the gas-phase l scale.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The linear blowoff branch may lend itself to extrapolation of normal-gravity flammability testing to zero stretch to estimate the lower microgravity flammability limit.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Gas sensor data and rod mass loss estimates indicate that the flames are globally stoichiometric at higher O2 concentrations but become more globally fuel rich as the minimum O2 concentration is approached.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This is due to excess pyrolyzate leakage out of the open tail of the hemispherical flames.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: CO production also increases significantly at low O2 levels.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The CO to CO2 ratio increases as well at low O2 concentrations.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This data suggests that the limiting reactant at the lowest O2 concentrations is the O2 rather than the fuel.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A critical Damköhler number formulation is applied across the flammability boundary, and the critical flame temperature is derived.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This critical flame temperature is used in a Nusselt number
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 90 correlation to estimate the convective heat flux to the stagnation region of the rod.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A surface energy balance is formulated that uses the critical flame temperature and convective heat flux to derive the mass burning rate along the boundary.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The rod regression rates calculated from this model compare favorably with the experimental measurements.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The terms of the surface energy balance are compared and reveal that in the blowoff branch, heat losses are negligible.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In the quenching region, surface radiative loss dominates.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Solid conductive loss down the rod is lower and decreases with decreasing stretch due to the low Peclet number.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Gas-phase radiative feedback becomes an important heat transfer process that extends the flammability limit to lower a.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: At the bottom of the flammability map, heat losses are only 30 percent of the total heating rate to the surface, so the transition from blowoff to quenching occurs when the convective flows become the same order of magnitude as diffusive flows, shifting the critical Damköhler number residence time limitations to diffusive time limitations.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The transport of the limiting reactant O2 is limited by concentration gradients, causing the needed ambient O2 to increase as the a is reduced.

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 93 7.0 Individual Principal Investigator Report: T’ien 7.1 Concurrent Flame Growth, Spread, and Extinction Over Composite Fabric Samples in Low-Speed Purely Forced Flow in Microgravity3 7.1.1 Abstract As a part of the NASA Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) and BASS–II experimental projects aboard the International Space Station, flame growth, spread, and extinction over a composite cotton-fiberglass fabric blend (referred to as the SIBAL (Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low Speed) fabric) were studied in low-speed concurrent forced flows.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The tests were conducted in a small flow duct within the Microgravity Science Glovebox.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The fuel samples measured 1.2 and 2.2 cm wide and 10 cm long.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Ambient O2 was varied from 21 percent down to 16 percent and flow speed from 40 cm/s down to 1 cm/s.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A small flame resulted at low flow, enabling us to observe the entire history of flame development including ignition, flame growth, steady spread (in some cases), and decay at the end of the sample.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition, by decreasing flow velocity during some of the tests, low-speed flame quenching extinction limits were found as a function of O2 percentage.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The quenching speeds were found to be between 1 and 5 cm/s with higher speed in lower O2 atmosphere.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The shape of the quenching boundary supports the prediction by earlier theoretical models.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These long-duration microgravity experiments provide a rare opportunity for solid fuel combustion since microgravity time in ground-based facilities is generally not sufficient.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This is the first time that a low-speed quenching boundary in concurrent spread is determined in a clean and unambiguous manner.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 7.1.2 Introduction Flame spread and extinction over condensed fuels in a microgravity environment has been the subject of extensive theoretical and experimental studies due to the importance of fire safety in human space missions (Refs.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Compared with burning in normal gravity, diffusion flames in microgravity are not affected by buoyancy-induced flow, thus providing a chance to study the fundamental mechanism(s) of low-speed flame quenching (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Transition from solid diffusion flame spreading to quenching extinction is a slow heat loss process characterized by a relative increase in the rates of radiative and conductive heat losses compared to the rate of heat generation (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Long-duration microgravity time is desired for such studies, which in general cannot be achieved by ground-based facilities.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Recently, NASA’s Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS and BASS–II) project examined the burning and extinction characteristics of a variety of solid fuel samples aboard the International Space Station (ISS).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Different thermally thin and thermally thick solid fuels were burned in concurrent, opposed, or stagnation flow configurations in a small flow duct.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Each experimental run took tens of seconds to minutes, depending on the sample type and flow conditions.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The challenge with thin solid samples in concurrent flow, compared with other configurations, is that flame spreads much faster, and flames can become quite long.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Because of size limitations, the fuel sample is relatively short and so a concurrent spreading flame may not reach fully steady spread within the sample length.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The transient ignition and flame growth process, however, provides a flame spread history that can be useful for the development of transient flame models (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In BASS–II, a N2 dilution scheme is used whereby the O2 percentage in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) can be decreased to a preset value so that flame spread can be 3Previously published by: Zhao, Xiaoyang; and T’ien, James S.: A Three-Dimensional Transient Model for Flame Growth and Extinction in Concurrent Flows.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 94 studied with O2 percentage as an additional variable parameter (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This facilitates the determination of the O2-flow-velocity flammability boundary of materials.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In this report, BASS and BASS–II results will be discussed in detail.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Flame growth, spread, and quenching extinction will be presented for a thin composite cotton-fiberglass fabric burning in various O2 concentrations and concurrent flow speeds.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 7.1.3 Experimental All tests were conducted in a small flow duct (shown in Figure 7.1) within the MSG aboard the ISS.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The sample used is a composite cotton-fiberglass fabric blend (75 percent cotton and 25 percent fiberglass).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The thickness of the sample is about 0.32 mm with an area density of 18.2 mg/cm2.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The fabric is custom made for a previous project Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low Speeds (SIBAL) (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 8), hence it is referred to here as the SIBAL fabric.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: One major advantage of this fuel sample is the retention of sample structure integrity after the combustible (i.e., cotton cellulose) is consumed because of the fiberglass mesh.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: It does not crack or produce curly ash typically seen in pure cellulose samples such as paper or cloth.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition to Reference 8, experimental studies using SIBAL fabric can be found in References 9 and 10.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In the experiment, SIBAL fuel samples of two different widths, 1.2 and 2.2 cm, were used.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The samples were mounted in stainless steel sample holders.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The fuel sample mounted to the holder was placed in the small flow duct of cross-sectional size 7.6 by 7.6 cm.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flow speed could be varied from 1 to 55 cm/s.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The tests were conducted in ambient O2 molar fraction of 16 to 21 percent.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: It should be noted that for a given test the O2 concentration was fixed while the flow speed could be varied.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A Kanthal® hot wire was used to ignite the fuel sample leading edge so that the flame can spread in a concurrent configuration.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flame growth process was recorded by two cameras.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The side-view video camera provided edge-on images of the flat samples at standard video framing rates (29.97 frames per second).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The top-view digital camera looked down on the top fuel surface and provided high-resolution still images of the flame at a rate of about one image every 1.2 s.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: When flow speed and O2 concentration were low, the flame became very dim blue and was difficult to see in the side video camera.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These still images provide a time history of flame quenching that can be used to compare with transient model results.

text: 7.1.4 Results and Discussion A total of 27 tests were carried out for the fabric samples in BASS–II, including six quenching tests, three nonignited tests, and one blowoff test.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition, four tests from the BASS series were selected as listed at the bottom of Table 7.1.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These four tests are all 21 percent O2 cases at a fixed flow velocity during each test.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For those cases with flow velocity variations, the starting and the final velocities are indicated in the velocity column.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The rate of velocity change varies from case to case depending on the communication between the astronauts and the ground crews and the manual adjustment time by the crew.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Many of these tests were used to determine the low-speed quenching limits as a function of O2 percentage.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In some tests, the flame quenched quickly or was not ignited.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These samples were reused in additional tests as indicated in Table 7.1.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Figure 7.5 shows a typical flame quenching sequence in the BASS–II experiment.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A 2.2-cm-wide sample in 18.7 percent O2 was first ignited at 10-cm/s flow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Flow speed was decreased to 2.2 cm/s incrementally after ignition.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Figure 7.6 shows flame tracking and flow speed versus time.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: After ignition, the flame started to grow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As the flow speed was reduced, both flame length and flame width dropped accordingly with flow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: After 25 s, flow velocity was reduced to 2.2 cm/s and held there for the remainder of the test.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As shown in Figure 7.5, both the flame length and flame width continued to decrease approaching a circular-shaped blue flame seen from the top.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The size of the flame continues to shrink until extinction is reached.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This is typical in a quenching extinction sequence.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As the quenching limit is approached (in this case by turning down the flow velocity), the fuel pyrolysis rate and combustion heat release rate (HRR) are reduced, and radiation loss becomes a significant fraction of the HRR from the shrinking flame.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: When the flame becomes small enough, conduction becomes the additional heat loss.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 101 7.1.5 Conclusions Concurrent flame growth and extinction over a thin flat cotton-fiberglass composite fabric sample was studied as part of the Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) and BASS–II space experiments aboard the International Space Station.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These long-duration microgravity experiments provided rare opportunities for solid fuel combustion studies.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: By reducing the flow velocity during the tests, quenching extinction limits were obtained accurately.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The quenching velocities are small (between 1 and 5 cm/s), and an accurate determination is necessary to resolve the slope of the quenching boundary.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The experimental data obtained supports earlier theoretical predictions (at least qualitatively) of solid flammability limits at low flow velocities due to radiative and conductive losses.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flame image sequence at quenching shows the flame shrinks both in length and width and the flame goes out in a three-dimensional manner.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition to obtaining quenching limits, the sequence of sample ignition, flame growth, and steady spread to final decay across the entire sample in low-speed purely forced flows were experimentally recorded.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These are precious data to help us to understand the entire process of flame development in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: They also provide the basis to check the theoretical model development.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Currently, we are measuring and deducing the pyrolysis rate constants for Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low Speeds (SIBAL) fabric in order to perform quantitative comparisons between the model and experiment.

text: D.3 Purpose of the Analysis Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS–II) samples are larger than previously flown samples, and there is a concern that the hardware will become overheated and be damaged by the burning of these large samples.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This analysis is to estimate the temperature rise of the BASS experiment assembly for a worst-case flame for this large thick sample.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: It should be noted that we have no plans to run a test like this.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Assumptions: • Th e worst-case sample is the 0.5-cm-thick, 8.5-cm-long, and 2-cm-wide polymethylmethacrylate (P MMA) slab sample. • Th e worst-case flame is a concurrent flame, which is expected to be larger than an opposed flame.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 122 Figure D.1.—Predicted flame temperature profile for flame in forced flow velocity U of 60-cm/s flow, from Reference 1.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: D.4 Background The basis for the burning rate estimates presented here are based on both a computational study looking at the burning rate distribution for boundary layer flow combustion of a PMMA plate in forced flow, shown in Figure D.1, (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 1), and BASS test results from a 1-cm PMMA sphere burning in a stagnation flow (which captures the burning of the exposed base of the sample).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A thick PMMA slab will take time to ignite and grow to a steady-state size, and the sample burning rate distribution is an important quantity to determine how much heat is being generated by the flame.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: D.5 Analysis As can be seen in Figure D.2, the base of the flame (at x = 0) has the highest burning rate and there is an exponential decay in the regression rate away from that peak burning rate.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Using peak regression rate (rmax) for the four flow profiles given, we can extrapolate down to the 30-cm/s flow of interest.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The exposed base of the flame (the upstream most point) will be the strongest part of the flame, and the burning rate is expected to be a maximum there.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Based on data in the Section D.7 from a 1-cm-sphere BASS test, we estimate the regression rate to be 3.05 mm/min, which is in keeping with the estimates from Figure D.2, as shown in Figure D.3.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The downstream regression rates will decay exponentially from there, as shown in Figure D.2.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 123 Figure D.2.—Peak regression rates from Figure D.2 curve fit with expected square root trend as flow is reduced (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Fit is used to calculate extrapolated points.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: At 30 cm/s, peak regression rate is estimated to be 3.13 mm/min.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Figure D.3.—Power law growth pattern used to predict flame size as function of time.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The sample is 8.5 cm long, so at 3.05 mm/min, it will take ~28 min for the flame base to regress the entire length of the sample.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Note that this is way beyond the still camera card limit of 7 min.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flame will take some time to grow the steady-state size.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: To estimate the growth rate, we use an expected power law growth rate (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 3) and estimate the flame will grow to a steady-state size in approximately 2.5 min, as shown in Figure D.3.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This growth rate is quite reasonable, since a previous BASS test showed that a PMMA slab sample took over 3 min to grow to steady size, as shown in the Section D.7.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Using the experimental growth history and peak regression rates, we can estimate the regression rate profiles as a function of time.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These regression profiles (which occur on both sides of the sample) can then be used to determine how much fuel is being consumed each minute.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: We do this by adding up the regression at each x location (basically, the area under the curves) and also multiplying that value by the width of the sample (2 cm).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Note that these profiles are derived from steady slab burning where a significant fraction of the heat release is returned to the fuel for preheating or reradiated to the environment.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 126 The maximum burn time is assumed to be the 2.5-min growth phase plus the 28-min sample regression phase, for a total of 30.5 min, as plotted in Figure D.5.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The maximum temperatures reported in the following information are for this maximum burn time.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The heat release in the early phase is dominated by the ignition energy.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Once the combustion heat release approaches steady state, the igniter is turned off and the flame is sustained.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The maximum temperature will occur in the exhaust hardware.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This metal (primarily copper) hardware is built to take the hot combustion gases and cool via conduction to the other hardware.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The maximum temperature if all of the combustion energy is only deposited in this heat sink under these worst-case assumptions, is 434 °C, which is below the melting point of the lowest melting material (aluminum at 660 °C) so this absolute worst-case maximum temperature will not cause damage to the hardware.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This maximum temperature will not be realized in actuality because the heat will quickly dissipate to the main housing, which reaches a maximum temperature of 110 °C if all of the heat is distributed only there.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The experiment assembly dissipates the heat further, and the maximum temperature of the entire experiment assembly is 62 °C.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: During the 10-min cooldown for these thick samples, both the flow through the BASS duct and the MSG air circulation fans help dissipate the heat.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The MSG air cooling loop has a 125-W capacity, which would dissipate the energy in 18 min, assuming no dissipation via conduction to the MSG hardware.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Based on this worst-case analysis, it is not expected that the hardware will suffer any damage from the worst-case, largest flames that could be achieved with the BASS–II samples.

text: Microgravity experiments burning cast PMMA cylindrical rods in axial flow have been conducted aboard the International Space Station in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) facility using the Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS) flow duct, as part of the BASS-II experiment.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: Twenty-four concurrent-flow tests were performed, focusing on finding flammability limits as a function of oxygen and flow speed.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: The oxygen was varied by using gaseous nitrogen to vitiate the working volume of the MSG.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: The speed of the flow parallel to the rod was varied using a fan at the entrance to the duct.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: Both blowoff and quenching limits were obtained at several oxygen concentrations.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: Each experiment ignited the rod at the initially hemispherical stagnation tip of the rod, and allowed the flame to develop and heat the rod at a sufficient flow to sustain burning.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: For blowoff limit tests, the astronaut quickly turned up the flow to obtain extinction.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: Complementary 5.18-second Zero Gravity Facility drop tests were conducted to compare blowoff limits in short and long duration microgravity.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: For quenching tests, the flow was incrementally turned down and the flame allowed to stabilize at the new flow condition for at least the solid-phase response time before changing it again.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: Quenching was observed when the flow became sufficiently weak that the flame could no longer provide adequate heat flux to compensate for the heat losses (conduction into the rod and radiation).
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: A surface energy balance is presented that shows the surface radiative loss exceeds the conductive loss into the rod near the limit.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: The flammability boundary is shown to represent a critical Damkohler number, expressed in terms of the reaction rate divided by the stretch rate.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: For the blowoff branch, the boundary exhibits a linear dependence on oxygen concentration and stretch rate, indicating that the temperature at blowoff must be fairly constant.
doc_title: Microgravity Flammability of PMMA Rods in Concurrent Flow

text: For the quenching branch, the dominance of the exponential nature of the Arrhenius kinetics reaction rate indicates that the temperature is critical.

text: 1.1 Background BASS–II tests the hypothesis that materials in microgravity, with adequate ventilation, burn as well if not better than the same material in normal gravity with other conditions being identical (pressure, O2 concentration, temperature, etc.).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA tests and controls materials from a flammability perspective using an upward burning test in normal gravity, which is considered to be the worst-case geometry for flammability of the material on Earth.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: However, it may not be conservative for flammability in space.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: One objective of the BASS–II tests is to identify what is the worst case for material flammability in spacecraft environments, and how does that compare to the terrestrial upward burning used to screen the materials for safe use aboard spacecraft.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Detailed combustion models can be validated by data obtained in the simpler flow environment in microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Once validated, they can be used to build more complex combustion models needed to capture the important details of flames burning in normal gravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These models have wide applicability to the general understanding of many terrestrial combustion problems.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The main variables tested were the effects of ambient O2 concentration, ventilation flow velocity, and fuel type, thickness, and geometry.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Many of the tests focused on finding a minimum O2 concentration or flow velocity where a material will burn in space, to compare with the Earth-based limits.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Flame growth rates are also of interest, to determine how quickly a fire in space can grow and if the flames reach a finite size or continue to grow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This has implications for firefighting strategies in spacecraft.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: BASS–II utilized the gaseous nitrogen (GN2) available on International Space Station (ISS) to vitiate the atmosphere in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) from standard ISS “air” down to the low O2 flammability limits.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: BASS–II also utilized onboard O2, CO, and CO2 sensors to evaluate the completeness of the combustion.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A total of 126 tests were conducted as part of BASS–II.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This is more than the planned 103 tests, since some samples were burned more than once.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: There are some samples that could be burned further, should future operational time become available.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For the first time on ISS, BASS–II utilized MSG working volume vitiation with GN2.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: We developed a perfectly stirred reactor model to determine the GN2 flow time and flow rate to obtain the desired reduced O2 concentration in the working volume for the tests.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This worked out extremely well for operations, and added a new vital variable, ambient O2 level, to our test matrices.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 1.2 Experiment Description The MSG in the Destiny Lab of the ISS provides a contained atmosphere in which fire safety experiments can be conducted (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The MSG, shown in Figure 1.1, has a set of filter banks that capture particulates and convert the CO to CO2 using an ambient temperature catalyst.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The BASS–II hardware is shown inside the MSG working volume in Figure 1.1.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 4 Figure 1.1.—Microgravity Science Glovebox Facility (MSG) working volume aboard the International Space Station (ISS) with the Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS– II) experiment hardware installed.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Working volume of MSG was diluted using ISS N2 gas.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Compound Specific Analyzer-Combustion Products (O2 and CO) and Carbon Dioxide Monitor (CO2) sensors were used to obtain before and after burn gas concentrations.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The BASS–II hardware consists of a flow duct, still camera, video camera, video and power boxes, external control box and associated plumbing, and mounting systems.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The black anodized 7.6- by 7.6- by 17-cm rectangular flow duct with rounded corners was originally built to perform gas jet diffusion flame studies (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: It was adapted to accommodate solid samples for the BASS experiments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flow was blown through the duct using a variable speed fan.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Two additional flow restrictors could be used at the fan inlet to increase the pressure drop and thus reduce the flow through the duct to the desired value for the test point.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: With no restrictors, the maximum flow velocity was ~55 cm/s, and with two restrictors this was reduced to ~35 cm/s.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flow then passed through a honeycomb flow straightener and an inlet screen to reduce swirl.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: An omnidirectional spherical airspeed transducer (TSI Incorporated 8475) was positioned between the honeycomb and the screen and was used to measure the steady-state flow through the duct.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The air velocity transducer probe had a response time of approximately 1 minute.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Inside the test section was a nozzle for N2 flow, a movable scale, and an Oriel® 71768 thermopile detector (Newport Corporation) with a CaFl window (spectral range of 0.13 to 11 μm) in the downstream top back corner of the duct viewing the upstream direction.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The test section of the duct had two orthogonal windows; the top one was replaced for BASS to provide a mounting rail system for the solid samples.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The top window was used by a Nikon D300s 12.3-megapixel digital color still camera with a 60-mm lens that provided 4,320- by 2,968-pixel images.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The duct exit contained a perforated copper plate followed by a brass screen to provide heat rejection and a cold surface for soot deposition.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flow turned 90° to exit the duct, which facilitated mixing of the hot combustion gases with the cool ambient air.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The front window also had interlocks for the igniter and N2 flow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A Panasonic Corporation color video camera
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The video camera had an overlay that displayed the N2 flow rate (cm3/min), fan voltage (10× V), air velocity transducer reading (cm/s), and the radiometer signal.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The fan voltage was calibrated with the airspeed transducer at the end of every operations day.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The radiometer signal was not calibrated but provided a measure of the flame dynamics and steadiness.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The external control box had controls for the fan voltage, N2 flow rate, enable switches for the igniter and N2 flow, and a radiometer gain level setting.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A number of sample geometries were used in BASS–II: cast polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) samples were shaped as rods of various diameters (6.35 to 12.7 mm), thin to thick slabs (0.125 to 5 mm), or a section of a 4-cm-diameter sphere.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition, flat cotton-fiberglass blended fabric samples were also burned.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These samples could generally be mounted so that they could be burned in either the opposed or concurrent flow direction.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The samples were manually ignited with a Kanthal® A–1 29-gauge hot-wire igniter coil with a nominal hot wire resistance of 0.8 to 1 Ω, powered by 3.5 to 3.8 amps when the astronaut manually pulled the deployment lever to move the igniter into position.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Samples were burned within the duct and the combustion products exited the duct and mixed with the gas in the work volume.

text: To evaluate the levels of combustion products produced during microgravity fires, BASS–II requested the use of available onboard sensors to measure the O2 depletion and the completeness of combustion (CO and CO2) for microgravity combustion tests under spacecraft ventilation flow rates to provide scientific data on the stoichiometry of the diffusion flame reactions and heat release rates (HHRs).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The data reported here is the first extensive data on the stoichiometry and toxicity of combustion products in microgravity.

text: 1.3 Validation of Microgravity Science Glovebox Dilution—Continuously Stirred Tank Reactor Model To utilize the capabilities of MSG to reduce the O2 in the working volume in a controlled manner, a dilution model based on a continuously stirred tank reactor (CSTR) model was developed.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In this model, the mixing in the working volume (via the BASS–II duct fan) is assumed to be “instantaneous,” so that the outflow “leak” concentration from the MSG work volume to the ISS cabin is the perfectly mixed instantaneous concentration.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This perfect mixing approximation is valid as long as the residence time (volume per flow rate or V/R) is at least 5 to 10 times as long as the mixing time, which is met by the 100 LPM N2 flow rate during dilution (250 liters/100 LPM ~ 2.5 min mixing time).
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For the MSG volume and N2 flow rates, the working volume residence time is V/R = 500+ min, and the mixing time is shorter than 50 min, so the assumption is valid.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The model assumes the work volume is at constant pressure and temperature and constant volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Thus, the leak rate out of the work volume is equal to the rate of N2 supplied (r).

text: 1.6 Overall Conclusions As part of the Burning and Suppression of Solids—II (BASS–II) experiment, we conducted a number of tests with different geometries, flow velocities, and initial O2 concentrations.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The last variable was enabled using gaseous N2 to dilute the working volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: To adequately characterize this dilution, we developed a continuously stirred tank reactor model and verified it against sensor readings.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Sensor data from the tests showed that the O2 was burning nearly stoichiometrically to CO2, and that CO levels appear to be a function of geometry and, in some cases, the flow velocity and geometry combination.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The CO to CO2 ratios for these fires are an order of magnitude higher than for efficient flue gases, indicating that these flames are not efficient.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The heat release was estimated for the tests using O2 consumption calorimetry.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This showed that most of the tests released well below 100 W.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In the one long test that released close to 100 W, we sustained some damage to the downstream corner of the front window, due to a leak that directed the heat from this energetic flame to that location during the prolonged burn.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Using the mass loss and O2 consumption data, the global equivalence ratio for the tests is estimated to be 1.3 on average, which indicates the flames were burning fuel rich under the low-velocity forced-flow conditions.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 2.1.2.1 Extinction Velocity Each test is started by establishing a steady flame spread in the presence of a forced flow and then reducing the flow velocity in a gradual manner, as shown in Figure 2.1.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In the first test, a steady flame was established over a 100-μm sample.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: After the flame propagated across half the sample length at a steady spread rate of 2.2 mm/s, the flow was abruptly cut off and the flame was observed to extinguish within 2 s, as shown by the radiometer signal drop in Figure 2.2.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: To pin down the extinction flow velocity, a second test was done under the same conditions except the flow velocity was set at 3 cm/s and after the flame propagated about half the sample length, the flow was gradually reduced.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The flame spread rate of the leading edge, as plotted in Figure 2.3, shows that the flame extinguishes at about 30 s after ignition.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The fan voltage at that time indicates a flow velocity of about 1.1 cm/s.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The sequence of images in Figure 2.1 shows the pathway to radiative extinction.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As the flow speed is gradually reduced from about t = 27 s, the flame size starts shrinking and the orange color disappears and the flame becomes completely blue, most possibly because of the temperature drop brought about by radiative losses, which is enhanced by the increased residence time at low flow velocity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The signal from the radiometer, shown in Figure 2.2, is also consistent with a cooling and shrinking flame as the signal starts decreasing from right about t = 27 s.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: After t = 30 s, there is no visible flame and the radiometer data (Figure 2.2) indicate a sudden change in slope at that time, possibly because the radiation is emitted mostly by the sample holder with the combustion products swept away by the flow.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 2.3.5 Microgravity and Normal-Gravity Experiments There are only a handful of experiments conducted on flame spread in a microgravity environment, an excellent review of which can be found as a book chapter by T’ien (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The only long-duration opposed-flow experimental facility is offered by the BASS–II apparatus (Ref.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: It is a combustion tunnel, a 76-mm square duct, where the PMMA (C2H8O2) fuel samples, 20 mm wide and about 95 mm long with the thickness ranging from 100 to 400 μm, are burned in an opposed-flow configuration.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A fan forces a flow of an O2-N2 mixture through flow straighteners from the right to the left and the sample, 2 cm wide, is ignited at the left end.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Depending on the flow velocity and O2 concentration, a steady flame is established that spreads from the left end of the sample towards the right end.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The oxidizer mixture consists of O2 and N2 where the O2 level can be adjusted at 21 percent or below.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: During the experiment, an O2 sensor monitors the O2 level, which has been found to drift by less
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A hot wire anemometer is used to calibrate the flow velocity with the voltage of the fan (see Figure 2.16) used for creating a flow of 50 cm/s or below.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The total pressure is also monitored, which varied from 99.2 to 99.5 kPa in the tests reported.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Experiments were conducted in the Microgravity Science Glovebox of ISS by two crew members.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Operation instructions were communicated from NASA Glenn Operations Center in realtime as the experiment progressed.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Each test starts by creating a desired opposing flow by adjusting the fan voltage.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: After the flow stabilizes, the igniter is turned on until a visible flame is observed.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The igniter is then turned off and the top view of the flame propagation is photographed with a high-resolution digital still camera with a frame rate of 1 per second.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A video camera captures the side view of the flame propagation.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In some of the tests, the flow velocity is changed during the spread to maximize the test matrix without having to burn additional samples.

text: 2.3.7 Results and Discussion The average spread rate over the 100-μm-thick sample in the normal-gravity experiments is found to be 2.0 mm/s (see Figure 2.19(b)).

doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Any variation is probably due to surface irregularities and other random factors.

doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 47 4.0 Individual Principal Investigator Report: Fernandez-Pello 4.1 Opposed-Flame Spread Task The scientific objective of the Burning and Suppression Solids—II (BASS–II) opposed-flow flame spread test is to further understand the mechanisms controlling the spread of flames over the surface of solid combustible materials, particularly in a spacecraft environment.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For this purpose, experiments were conducted aboard the International Space Station (ISS) to determine the effects of microgravity on the spread of flames over polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) rods of different diameters subjected to different O2 concentrations and low flow velocities.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: These are parameters that in addition to low pressure are expected in spacecraft environments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: By conducting these tests aboard the ISS and then comparing the results to ground-based data, it is expected that a better understanding of the governing mechanisms of flame spread in microgravity can be obtained.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition, by conducting the tests with cylindrical samples, the effect on the flame spread process of geometrical factors such as the transverse curvature of the surface can be better studied.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: 4.1.1 Experiment and Test Matrix The tests were conducted in the BASS–II hardware placed inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) in the Destiny Lab of the ISS.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The BASS–II hardware consists of a flow duct, still camera, video camera, external control box, and associated plumbing and mounting systems along with the fuel samples for the BASS–II experiments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The tests for the present task were conducted with rods of cast PMMA with diameters of 6.35, 9.525, and 12.7 mm (1/4, 3/8, and 1/2 in., respectively) and were 57.15 mm in length.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: All cylindrical rods tested started with rounded (hemispherical) ends in order to minimize the flow disturbance associated with the abrupt bluff body transition at the sample’s downstream edge.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Ignition of the PMMA was accomplished by using a hot wire placed to heat the PMMA surface in the downstream edge of the rods.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Table 4.1 and Table 4.2 present the test conditions for the opposed-flow flame spread tests conducted in this task.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The majority of the tests were conducted with black PMMA, because rods of black PMMA are also used in the Material Ignition and Suppression Test (MIST) project to reduce effects of in-depth absorption of thermal radiation.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: For this reason, the results presented in this report are limited to those for black PMMA.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: A few tests were conducted with clear PMMA for comparison purposes, but the data is too limited to present it here.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In comparing the experimental results from ground-based experiments with those conducted aboard the ISS, a number of complications arise.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: First and foremost, due to the effect of buoyancy, the effective opposed-flow velocity felt by the flame in the 1g experiments is an order of magnitude greater than the velocities tested in microgravity experiments.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: As has been shown elsewhere, the difference in flame spread rate between natural convective conditions and an opposed-flow velocity of 0.25 m/s in 1g is relatively negligible.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: On the other hand, for the microgravity tests presented herein, the flow velocities under investigation are near the quenching limit, below those normally expected from the air supply and recirculation systems currently employed on the ISS.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In addition to difficulties regarding the use of comparable flow velocities, in the microgravity experiments only the two largest diameter rods were tested at near 21 percent O2 by volume, with the highest O2 concentration tested for the 6.35-mm-diameter rods being approximately 19 percent by volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: The only O2 concentration at which all three rod diameters employed in the microgravity experiments were tested was at approximately 17.5 percent O2 by volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In the 1g experiments, the lowest O2 concentration at which all four tested rod diameters were successfully burnt without the addition of an external radiant heat source was 19 percent by volume.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Thus, in comparing the datasets, some compromises were made.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: In particular, as can be seen in Figure 4.3, the ranges of O2 concentrations and rod diameters employed do not completely overlap.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: Yet, the trend in flame spread rate in terms of both O2 concentration and rod diameter are still quite apparent even after discounting the fact that the flow velocities are not strictly comparable.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: NASA/TM-20210011385 50 The most important result of the comparison is that of the minimum O2 concentration for flame spread in normal and microgravity.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: While in microgravity, flame spread was observed at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, in normal gravity, flame spread was not observed below 19 percent.
doc_title: Burning and Suppression of Solids–II  (BASS-II) Summary Report

text: This result is probably due to the lower opposed-flow velocity in the microgravity tests in comparison with those induced by buoyancy in normal gravity.
