text: CIR’s Low -Light-Level Ultraviolet (LLL-UV) package is a monochrome camera with an intensifier (for 280-700 nm) and a 310-nm bandpass filter (wit h a 10-nm FWHM) for OH* imaging.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Again as a result of the signal loss through the filter, binning is employed such that the OH* images are recorded at 512x512 and 30 fps.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The ACME chamber insert will also be equipped with non-imaging optical diagnostics including both thermopile radiometers and P hotomultiplier Tubes (PMTs).
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: There is a crew-exchangeable linear array of radiometers of which ther e are two versions supporting the initial set of experiments.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The array has a fixed position which is parallel to the chamber axis and centered (along the chamber length) relative to th e chamber windows and thus most of the other
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: One array is equipped with a sing le wide-view radiometer with two narrowview radiometers that are downstream and two more that are upstream, where all views are orthogonal to the chamber axis, as depicted in Figure 4.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The narrow-view radiometers are intended to support studies of gas-jet flames, where ACME can accommodate shorter burners, making the “lower” detectors useful.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: 4, provides for three wide-view measurements of the flame, where one view is masked to nominally block radiant emission from the burner.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: It was specifically designed for the BRE experiment but will be a resource available to other ACME experiments.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Given that the radiometer array can be exchanged by the crew, alternate arrays could be developed.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Figure 4: Crew-exchangeable radiometer arrays on the ACME chamber insert: (top) standard (ACME) array of 5 radiometers, and (bottom) array with three radiometers, designed for the BRE experiment, where the lowest detector is masked to avoid view of the burner.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: 10 An additional wide-view radiometer, that is fixe d and not crew exchangeable, is positioned downstream of the burner and flame at 30 o from the chamber axis.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: This detector is primarily intended to support the spherical flame experimen ts and will have a quicker response than the more sensitive detectors that will used in the linear arrays.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Like the radiometers on the two linear arrays, it will have a spectral range of nominally 0.2-11 micron and its field of view will be established by an appropriately selected aperture.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: To detect the quenching of dim flames, the cham ber insert will be equipp ed with a set of three PMTs.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Each PMT will have a wide-angle view, a sight line that is orthogonal to the chamber axis, and will be centered (along the chamber length) re lative to the chamber windows so that it is aligned with most of the other instrumentation.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The PMTs’ spectral range will be 230-700 nm, i.e., visible and near ultraviolet, but one will have a 310-nm bandpass filter and another will have a 430-nm bandpass filter (where both are with a 10-nm FWHM).
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The pair of detectors will enable measurement of OH* and CH* emission, respectively.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The third PMT will be equipped with a neutral density filter to prevent saturation.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Like many other components, the PMT array can be removed from the chamber insert by the crew.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The chamber insert is also e quipped with six far-field thermocouples to measure the spread of the thermal field in the spherical flame experiments.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: They are of limited utility for other experiments because they are positioned upstream of the burner tip.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Therefore, they will generally not be installed by the crew to reduce the chance of accidental damage.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: There will be two versions of a four-thermocouple rake to allow a choice of near and far measurements.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Other arrays could be designed to support future experiments, but they cannot extend downstream of the burner tip without interfering with other (e.g., optical) measurements.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Experiment-unique hardware is a lso mounted on the chamber inser t.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: For example, to accommodate the E-FIELD Flames experiment, the insert is equipped with a high-voltage supply and a crew-removable electrode mesh which can be set between +10 and -10 kV.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The circular mesh is orthogonal to the chamber axis and is positioned (during set up) at either ~35 or ~50 mm downstream of the insulated burner.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The ion current between the burner and electrode mesh will be determined via measurement of the voltage drop across a known resistor and application of Ohm’s Law.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Additional supporting measurements will be made, where the chamber pressure is a simple example.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The ACME experiments will use the CIR’s gas chromatograph for pre- and post-test analysis of the chamber atmosphere, e. g., for oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and fuel gases.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Acceleration measurements will be provided by the Space Acceleration Measurement System (SAMS) [27], which is the primary instrument for such measurements on ISS and previously served that role for the space shuttle.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: All ACME experiments will be constant volume (i.e., rather than consta nt pressure) studies, where the chamber’s free volume will be about 90 liters.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Burner flows will generally be constrained to limit the pressure rise, and tests will typically be 0.5-2 minutes in duration.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The ACME experiments will be configured, but not conducted, by the ISS crew.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Instead, the experiments will be commande d from the ground, specifically from the Telescience Support Center (TSC) at the NASA Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, Ohio.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: They can be conducted in a nominally automated mode using pre-programmed scripts.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: However, it will also be possible to effectively operate the experiments in a “manual” mode, where changes can be made in response to the analog video downlink and the numerical data available in the telemetry stream.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: 11 For example, a flow rate could be adjusted to a pproach a stability or soot li mit.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Step and ramp changes can be made in the flow rate(s) or e lectric field potential.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: The TFP fiber array can be translated uniformly through a soot-free flame to get a continuum measurement of the temperature field.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: In summary, ACME’s experiment control will allow for broad flexibility.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Concluding Remarks In January 2014, the Obama administration announ ced that ISS operations will continue until at least 2024.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: It is currently expected that the five ACME experiments will be conducted from 2016 to 2019.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: While there are plans for subsequent CIR experiments, e.g., to study flame spread across solid fuels, future experiments could be conducted using the ACME hardware.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Although the current ACME experiments are limited to laminar non-premixed flames, turbulent and burner-stabilized premixed flames could also be studied using the ACME chamber insert.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Many of the hardware elements are exchangeable on orbit, including for example, the burner, igniter arm and tip, video cameras, radiometer array, P MT array, TFP fiber array, thermocouple rake, high-voltage supply, electrode mesh, and the gas chr omatograph.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: As such, the hardware can be customized to support a wide variety of future ex periments.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: Gaseous flames could continue to burn brightly on the ISS.
doc_title: Gaseous Non-Premixed Flame Research Planned for the International Space Station

text: 9 BASS-II Science Overview Relevance/Impact: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II) tests the hypothesis that materials in microgravity, with adequate ventilation, burn as well if not better than the same material in normal gravity with other conditions being identical (pressure, oxygen concentration, temperature, etc.).
doc_title: SRD_BASS-II (planned tests, not results)

text: Objectives: • To identify what is the worst case for material flammability in spacecraft environments, and how does that compare to the terrestrial upward burning used to screen the materials for safe use aboard spacecraft. • To determine how quickly a fire in space can grow and if the flames reach a finite size or continue to grow.
doc_title: SRD_BASS-II (planned tests, not results)

text: This has implications for firefighting strategies in spacecraft.
doc_title: SRD_BASS-II (planned tests, not results)

text: Primary variables: The main variables to be tested are the effects of ambient oxygen concentration, ventilation flow velocity, and fuel type, thickness, and geometry.
doc_title: SRD_BASS-II (planned tests, not results)

text: Development Approach: BASS-II will utilize the on orbit BASS hardware launched originally for SPICE on STS-126.
doc_title: SRD_BASS-II (planned tests, not results)

text: New samples, igniters, and more flash cards will provide new data.
doc_title: SRD_BASS-II (planned tests, not results)
